scope: Standing Temple of the Inscriptions at Palenque, including its restored stepped pyramid, original north stair arrangement, small upper stair, roof comb fragments and sanctuary with five openings.
geometryBasis: Named ruin way 160083187 fixes the temple location and angle, the plaza side, and the shared west boundary with Temple XIII. The mapped visible outline is about 40 by 31 m. Published archaeological measurements report about 55 by 35 m for the wider base. The wider lower extent is fitted mainly east of the mapped center while preserving the shared west edge.
sectionBasis: INAH describes the tall north stepped front, six supporting piers and five doorways, and the surviving limestone stubs of the roof comb. Ruz measured 23.38 m by 7.70 m at the sanctuary, with an approximately 2 m podium and a nine-step stair. Filloy places the sanctuary floor about 24 m over the plaza. The 2007 and 2009 photographs fix the surviving gray limestone and visible north and east profiles.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: INAH identifies the north-facing pyramid, surviving nine-body construction phase, roof comb footings, five visible portals and remaining reliefs.
Field research records about 55 m east–west, 35 m north–south, about 30 m height and bedrock contact along the south and west.
The standing form has eight large exposed bodies to the terrace, the nine-step upper stair, a sanctuary floor about 24 m above the plaza, and a largely lost roof crest.
Ruz’s excavation report gives the upper body, base, portico and principal stair dimensions.
